bull_thesis: Prosus is a holding company whose main asset is a 22.8% stake in Tencent (about 2,066 million shares, worth roughly 106 billion euros at today's HK$460 Tencent price) — yet the whole company trades at an 84 billion euro market value. At 39.55 euros you are paying about 21% less than the Tencent stake alone, and the growing e-commerce portfolio — iFood (Brazil food delivery, revenue up 28% in fiscal 2026 with a 21% adjusted-EBITDA margin), OLX classifieds, PayU India, Just Eat, Despegar and a roughly 25% stake in Swiggy — comes for free at today's price. Management credibility on the profit turnaround is now demonstrated, not promised: e-commerce reached first-ever profitability in fiscal 2024 ahead of target, the CEO's fiscal-2025 pledge of 400 million dollars of adjusted EBITDA came in at 443 million, and fiscal 2026 (reported 29 June 2026) delivered about 1.3 billion dollars — roughly triple the prior year — on 9.7 billion dollars of ecosystem revenue, beating consensus on both earnings and revenue. The discount-compression engine is funded and running: the buyback has retired 46 billion dollars of stock to date (about a third of the free float), a further 5 billion dollar program was authorized for fiscal 2027, at least 2 billion dollars a year of non-core asset sales are committed, and the EU-mandated sale of the 27.4% Delivery Hero stake (a condition of the Just Eat approval) converts another chunk of the portfolio into buyback fuel — at Delivery Hero prices that have more than doubled off their low. Every share repurchased below net asset value mechanically raises value per share. The stock sits 2% off its 52-week low and 38% below its October high almost entirely because Tencent has fallen a third from its peak — the discount play is intact while the underlying operating story has only improved. Conditions that must hold: Tencent stabilizes (it remains a cash-generative AI-capable franchise paying Prosus over a billion dollars a year in dividends), the buyback keeps running at the announced pace, and iFood's Brazilian margins survive new competition.
bear_thesis: This has been 'cheap versus its parts' for a decade, and the discount has never durably closed — buying a melting anchor at a discount still loses money. Eighty-five percent of the asset value is a single Chinese stock in drawdown: Tencent is down about a third from its 52-week high amid a broad China tech de-rating, and if that continues, net asset value falls faster than any buyback can offset — the past nine months proved it, with Prosus falling from 64 to under 40 euros while the buyback ran at 6-7 billion dollars a year. Second, the operating portfolio's crown jewel is newly threatened: Meituan — whose own stock has nearly halved in a brutal Chinese food-delivery subsidy war — is expanding its Keeta delivery brand into Brazil, aiming directly at iFood's dominant share; a price war would compress the 21% margin that anchors the bull case's private-asset marks. Third, capital allocation risk is real and recent: management spent about 4.1 billion euros buying Just Eat Takeaway, a structurally stagnant asset management itself admits 'is not performing well', plus Despegar and La Centrale — the September-2025 balance sheet's 4.4 billion dollars of net cash was largely consumed by these deals, so the cash cushion in the scan data overstates today's position. Fourth, the screener's headline numbers flatter the story: the 200% net margin and 8.12 trailing earnings per share are inflated by one-off stake-sale gains and fair-value accounting, not operating profit — the standalone operating company is barely at cash-flow breakeven, and the 163.87 'fair value' in the scan (implying 337% upside) is a broken model output for a holding company. Fifth, the classifieds assets (OLX and the newly bought La Centrale) face a live generative-AI displacement question — the same fear that produced Rightmove's AI-related profit warning and the sector sell-off in late 2025. What confirms the bear case: Tencent breaking below its 52-week low, a Keeta-driven iFood margin reset, or the fiscal-2027 buyback being trimmed to fund another large acquisition.
sop_fair_value: 45 EUR (base-case net asset value of roughly 62 euros per share, less a 25-30% holding-company discount)
sop_breakdown: Per share, at today's live marks (2.13 billion shares outstanding, EUR/HKD 8.95): Tencent stake 22.8% (2,066 million shares at HK$460.20) = ~106 billion euros, or ~49.90 per share; other listed stakes (residual Delivery Hero position mid-forced-sale, ~25% of Swiggy worth ~1.6 billion euros, residual Meituan, small positions) = ~2.60 per share; unlisted e-commerce portfolio (iFood, OLX, PayU India, Just Eat at a haircut to its 4.1 billion euro cost, Despegar, eMAG, La Centrale, ventures) conservatively ~25 billion euros = ~11.70 per share; net central cash assumed roughly nil after the Just Eat settlement (the 4.4 billion dollar September-2025 net-cash figure predates that payment); capitalized central costs ~ -0.80 per share. Gross net asset value ~62 euros per share — consistent with the ~35% discount third parties measured in mid-June at a 39.48 price. Base case applies a residual 25-30% holding-company discount (justified by the permanent conglomerate structure, but tighter than today's level given the running buyback and profit inflection): ~45. Bear case: Tencent down a further 20%, private assets marked to ~18 billion euros, discount stays at 40%: ~30. Bull case: Tencent recovers 20% (roughly its 200-day average), private assets 30 billion euros, discount narrows to ~22%: ~58.
risk_reward: At 39.55 euros the stock trades below the live market value of its Tencent stake alone (about 49.90 per share), with the operating portfolio and cash effectively priced at less than zero. Downside to the adverse case at 30 euros requires both a further Tencent leg down and the discount staying at its widest; upside to the 45 euro base case requires no re-rating heroics — only Tencent holding its level and the discount reverting toward the middle of its own ten-year range while the buyback shrinks the share count. The favorable case near 58 euros needs a China tech recovery plus continued e-commerce profit delivery. The asymmetry comes from entry 2% above the 52-week low with the funded buyback bidding daily; the main way to lose from here is a continued single-asset (Tencent/China) decline, which no buyback pace can outrun.
peer_comps_note: The peer frame is holding companies at a discount to net asset value (Naspers, Bollore) with the underlying assets benchmarked against Sea, MercadoLibre and Grab. The live anchor multiple is the NAV discount itself: about 36% today versus a 40-50% historical extreme and roughly 25-30% at the tights earlier in 2026 — so Prosus is at the cheap end of its own range but not at an unprecedented level. The scan's 49.7x price-to-free-cash-flow and 200% net margin are notional holding-company artifacts (stake sales, fair-value gains), not operating economics; parent Naspers trades at a further discount on top of Prosus, confirming the structural nature of the gap. Versus the operating peers, iFood's 28% growth at a 21% adjusted-EBITDA margin stands comparison with MercadoLibre's commerce economics, which supports — but does not prove — the private-asset marks.
forcing_function: There is no single hard-dated event that forces the discount closed; the engine is continuous. The dated items on the calendar: the EU-mandated sell-down of the 27.4% Delivery Hero stake (a binding condition of the Just Eat clearance of 11 August 2025, originally a 12-month window, since extended — proceeds recycle into the buyback); the fiscal-2027 buyback of 5 billion dollars announced 29 June 2026, running open-ended against an 84 billion euro market value; management's commitment to at least 2 billion dollars a year of further non-core disposals with more to be named within about six months; and half-year results due around late November 2026, the first print to show a full period of Just Eat under Prosus ownership. The most recent hard catalyst — the 29 June 2026 annual results, which beat on both earnings and revenue — has already fired without producing a re-rating, which is the clearest evidence that the market is currently trading this on Tencent's tape, not on Prosus's own delivery.
moderator_conclusion: This is a real discount with a credible, funded compression engine attached — and a single dominant risk that the engine cannot control. The forensic record supports management: across five earnings calls the CEO set numeric profit targets and beat them each time (400 million dollars promised, 443 delivered in fiscal 2025; 1.1-1.2 billion guided at the November 2025 half-year, about 1.3 billion delivered in fiscal 2026), the buyback has run exactly as promised, and the pivot to funding it by selling other assets rather than Tencent was announced and then executed. The valuation is genuinely below the sum of its parts: the price is under the liquid value of the Tencent stake alone. What keeps this at wait-rather-than-buy-now is timing, not thesis. The stock's fall is almost entirely a Tencent/China de-rating that is still in progress (Tencent fell 2% today), the catalyst set is soft and continuous rather than dated and binding, and the June results beat already fired into an indifferent tape. The disciplined entry is on evidence the single-asset slide has exhausted — Tencent holding above its 52-week low for a sustained stretch, or Prosus itself breaking the 37-euro area with the buyback still running — or on the next hard print in late November 2026. On pure value, catalyst aside, this earns a high grade: a growing asset base, demonstrated capital discipline, and a price below liquidation-style value; the score is tempered one notch because the private-asset marks are self-referential, the Just Eat purchase shows management can still spend billions on a weak asset, and a new Brazilian food-delivery price war could dent the crown jewel. Sizing should respect that this is, first and foremost, a leveraged bet on Tencent stabilizing.

skeptic_self.kill_fact: No disqualifier found, but three corrections were applied against primary sources: (1) the scan's net-cash add-back of 4.39 billion dollars (September 2025 balance sheet) predates the ~4.1 billion euro Just Eat settlement that closed in October-November 2025 — treating it as live cash would double count, so central net cash was set to roughly nil and my first-pass net asset value was trimmed from ~64 to ~62 euros per share, in line with the ~35% discount third parties measured in mid-June 2026; (2) the scan's headline fair value of 163.87 (337% margin of safety) and the 200% net margin are broken holding-company artifacts driven by one-off gains and were discarded, not averaged in; (3) the bear case was widened for Meituan's Keeta entering Brazil against iFood and for the residual Delivery Hero/Meituan stakes being mid-sale (carried at conservative marks). None of these flips the thesis: even after all trims the price remains below the live value of the Tencent stake alone.
